$comment: Spec 19 R19-14 mandatory-row manifest. Each row names a class the requirement lists with MUST, the workflow that carries it, and the exact step name inside that workflow. scripts/check_mandatory_rows.py resolves every row and fails if the step does not exist or if its workflow never runs on a protected push (main/master). A row that is satisfied only by a pull_request-triggered workflow is a VIOLATION: R19-14 says these checks run on every protected push and release candidate.

rows.step: Web fail-closed middleware + REST authorization row
rows.reason: Fail-closed middleware is the row every other security assertion is layered on; if it is skipped, each downstream row measures a weaker server than production runs.
Full-history secret scan. A protected push is the last point at which a leaked credential can be refused before it is on the default branch.
R19-16 names 'registry fallback' among the conditions a release MUST fail on; the credential registry must be proven to refuse rather than degrade on every protected push.
A readiness endpoint that reports ready for a control that cannot run keeps a broken instance in rotation; it is a deployment gate, so it runs on every protected push.
Package inventory: a module that escapes enumeration is never built or tested, and the omission is invisible because the run is green over the modules it did find.

rows.step: Run every enumerated Python test suite
rows.reason: Nonzero test floor (R19-12). A suite that collects zero tests still exits 0 unless the floor is enforced, so the floor must run wherever the suite runs.
